messages:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated reserved pool `dp-stellar-1` at 100% reserved occupancy for tenant StellarBank. queue_length=12,300, queued_requests/s=420, 99th_latency=2.1s. Autoscaler errors: quota_exceeded / allocation_rejected. Pager triggered for enterprise tier. Link: https://ops.redwood/alerts/5067891234

Devon: ack, I'm on it — paging SRE Lead and infra.

Maya: joining. @Amy (CS) can you prep customer comms?

SRE Lead: hypothesis — autoscaler hit cloud GPU quota + noisy sessions in reserved pool preventing eviction. Need manual interventions: evict opportunistic sessions, apply short-term rate limits for non-critical routes, and request manual scale-up of pool.

Alex K: past 10m of scheduler logs show repeated allocation failures: `rpc allocator: AllocateGPU failed: Insufficient GPUs` then `autoscaler: api error 429 quota exceeded`. Also seeing high session churn from tenant=public-ingest.

Tom I: preparing manual actions. plan:
``` 
# evict low-priority sessions (non-enterprise)
rctl sessions evict --pool dp-stellar-1 --filter "tenant!=StellarBank and age>5m" --limit 500

# request manual scale
rctl pool scale dp-stellar-1 --add-gpus=8 --reason "pager - manual bump"
```
I'll run evict first.

Devon: running evict now...
```
> evict: scanned=18,200 sessions, matched=1,120, evicted=325, reclaimed_gpus=6
> note: 2 eviction workers throttled by rate limiter
```

Oncall Bot: autoscaler notice: manual-scaling-request queued, provider-API 429s dropping — queued for retry.

SRE Lead: good — after evictions, apply temporary routing caps to protect enterprise routes. Maya/Alex, push a rate-limit to non-essential embedding routes and set dedicate fallback for StellarBank to hosted-backend if latency spikes.

Alex K: pushed rule: `redwood route update --tenant StellarBank --limit 60rps --fallback hosted-small` — applied to model-pay-chat and pay-embed routes. Confirming rule propagation (2/3 regions).

Maya: contacting oncall for hosted fallback and letting CS know. Amy, any immediate customer feedback?

Amy (CS): StellarBank support reported elevated 5xxs and timeouts for model `pay-chat-bert` since 14:10. Impact: interactive UI timeouts and delayed batch scoring jobs. Customer-facing note drafted, will send after ops confirms timeline and mitigation.

Tom I: manual scale request retried and accepted by provider: +8 gpus provisioning. cluster control shows nodes registering.
```
> pool dp-stellar-1 capacity: before=32 GPUs, after=40 GPUs (provisioning 8)
> scheduler: reclaimable_gpus=6 + provisioning=8 => effective headroom ~14
```

Oncall Bot: queue length dropping: 12,300 -> 3,200 in 8m after evictions + scale. 95th latency trending down to 420ms.

Devon: running health checks. target for close: queue <200 && 95th <500ms for 5m.

SRE Lead: please record timeline and add postmortem owner. Devon owns postmortem. Action items: 1) investigate noisy-tenant detection & auto-eviction thresholds, 2) autoscaler quota handling (retry/backoff), 3) add conservative headroom for enterprise reserved pools, 4) improve alerts to surface early noisy neighbor patterns.

Amy (CS): sent customer note: apology + summary + mitigation actions + ETA for root-cause EOD. Customer asked for SLA credit assessment; I flagged to finance.

Devon: queue at 180, 95th=420ms, sustained for 6m. Marking incident RESOLVED in pager and beginning post-incident doc. Will open follow-ups: TICKET-INC-8421 (eviction tuning), TICKET-INC-8422 (autoscaler quota retries), TICKET-INC-8423 (pool headroom policy).

SRE Lead: nice run. We'll debrief tomorrow during incident retro. Thanks all.

Oncall Bot: Incident resolved. incident_id=2026-5067891234. Recording runbook trigger: manual-evict -> manual-scale -> route-cap -> CS notify.

Devon: I'll also schedule a short run to test forced eviction flow in staging and validate metrics.

Maya: adding notes to oncall rotation so next oncall sees updated steps.

Amy (CS): Customer confirmed receipt and asked for ETA on final RCA. I committed to EOD. :white_check_mark:

SRE Lead: closing channel. Thanks everyone.
